items.name: Salesforce
items.why: Exceptional Reo intent (195 events, 78 developers) plus this week’s Agentforce/AI-agent scale narrative and competitive pressure from DocuSign’s agent push. Not in Salesforce as a Modular customer—strong new-logo week.
items.message: Hi — noticing the continued focus on Salesforce’s AI agent labor market and Agentforce as a growth driver, including how peers like DocuSign are opening agent tools more broadly. As agent workloads multiply across CRM workflows, inference cost and latency become the constraint on how far you can push concurrency and response quality. Modular’s MAX inference engine is built for high-throughput LLM serving with strong GPU utilization, which teams use to keep agent fleets economical in production. Would it make sense to compare notes with the Agentforce infra owners for 30 minutes this week on serving costs and latency targets for your highest-volume agent paths?

items.name: DoorDash

items.message: Hi — InfoQ’s write-up on Flux running on the order of 130,000 engineering tasks through cloud-based agents stood out. At that volume, agent fleets live or die on inference throughput and unit economics as concurrency grows. Modular’s MAX engine helps teams serve LLM/agent workloads with lower latency and better GPU efficiency without rewriting the application layer. Given Walmart’s push into overlapping delivery categories, I imagine dispatch, support, and agent automation will keep scaling. Open to a short working session this week with the Flux/platform owners to map where serving cost or queueing is the bottleneck?

items.message: Hi — catching the coverage this week on Uber’s robotaxi strategy shift and the Delivery Hero buyout discussion. items.message: Hi — saw OpenEvidence launch its new medical AI model family and deepen the oncology agent push this week.
